newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac bid must not lower competition-ACCC.
newsitem.headline: Westpac bid must not lower competition-ACCC.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp must show that its proposed merger with the Bank of Melbourne Ltd would not lessen competition, Allan Fels, chairman of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Sunday.
"They will certainly have to show there is no reduction in competition, that is the challenge they face," Fels said in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday Business show.

Fels said Westpac would argue that it faces a lot of new competition particularly in the home lending market from the mortgage originators and that it will try to run the Bank of Melbourne as a regional bank.
Fels said the commission would take a few weeks to complete its inquiry into the proposed merger.
The A$1.435 billion merger is subject to the approval of the ACCC and federal treasurer Peter Costello.
Costello said on Thursday the fate of the agreed merger depended on the results of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, which is expected to be released next week.
The inquiry, headed by former Amcor Ltd chief executive Stan Wallis, is the first major review of the Australian finance sector regulations since the early 1980s.
Market enthusiasm for Westpac's bid waned on Friday due to fears that regulatory approval was not assured.
Bank of Melbourne shares ended the week at A$9.47, compared with Westpac's offer valuation of A$9.75 per share.
The Victoria-based bank's shares rose sharply ahead of the bid annoucement on Thursday.
The Australian Stock Exchange has begun an investigation into the share surge, with an exchange spokesman saying the timing of the merger announcement was under scrutiny.
